assessment.evidence: Independently re-simulated both policies from jobs.csv (12 jobs, total work 31) and cross-checked measure.sh awk logic. Every report number reproduces exactly. Schedules match row-for-row: FCFS A(0-9)...L(30-31); SJF B(0-1)...A(22-31), including tie-breaks (FCFS t=0 A before B by input order; SJF t=10 H before J by arrival). Means: FCFS 139/12=11.583333 wait, 170/12=14.166667 turnaround; SJF 48/12=4.000000 and 79/12=6.583333; equal differences 91/12=7.583333 confirmed. Tails: nearest-rank p95 = ceil(0.95*12)=12 (measure.sh rank logic int(11.4)+1=12 agrees), giving FCFS p95 turnaround 19 and SJF 31; max wait FCFS 18 (L, unique max), SJF 22 (A, unique max); report explains means-vs-tails divergence via SJF deferring job A. Fairness: worst-wait jobs L (wait 18, arrival 12/start 30) and A (wait 22, arrival 0/start 22) match schedules; report correctly distinguishes observed long waits from starvation (closed 12-job trace, all finish by t=31 under both). Recommendation: both constraint checks stated explicitly — FCFS p95 19<=22 pass but max wait 18>16 fail; SJF 31>22 and 22>16 both fail — and neither policy is adopted without relaxing limits, which is correct. Reproduce: data/method/validation rules described accurately (measure.sh exits 2 on bad header/NF/duration/dupes/non-12 rows), procedure, required results, and full metrics+schedule appendix retained and internally consistent (means to 6 decimals match %.6f output of 139/12, 170/12, 48/12, 79/12). Limits: all five SPEC items covered (n=12 collapses p95 to worst job, exact-duration assumption, single server, non-preemption, no production evidence). No discrepancies found; all conclusions follow from the trace.
